name: CHiME-3: Third CHiME Speech Separation and Recognition Challenge
description: CHiME-3 is a multichannel speech recognition and enhancement dataset recorded in real everyday noisy environments (cafes, buses, pedestrian areas, street corners) using a 6-channel tablet microphone array and a close-talking reference microphone across 14,658 utterances.

license.name: Custom Non-Commercial Challenge License
license.notes: Freely available for research and non-commercial evaluation purposes upon registration.

source_references.title: The Third 'CHiME' Speech Separation and Recognition Challenge: Analysis and Outcomes

verification.notes: Verified against Computer Speech & Language 2017 paper (DOI: 10.1016/j.csl.2016.10.005) and challenge documentation. Exactly 14,658 multichannel utterances: 8,738 training utterances (1,600 real + 7,138 simulated), 3,280 development utterances (1,640 real + 1,640 simulated), and 2,640 evaluation utterances (1,320 real + 1,320 simulated).

size.notes: Multi-channel 16 kHz 16-bit WAV files and prompt transcriptions.
